Rashi on Bava Kamma 26a:10:1.hebrew: איש כי יתן מום בעמיתו איש בעמיתו - הוי בדין נתינת מומין, ולא שור בעמיתו של בעליו:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 26a:10:1.english: [When] a man inflicts a blemish upon his fellow — a man against his fellow - [is included] in the law of inflicting blemishes, and not an ox against the fellow of its owner.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 26a:11:1.english: In the courtyard of the injured [party] - For the liability for Trampling is in the courtyard of the injured [party].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 26a:11:2.english: Here too it is no different - For Foot is forewarned from its beginning to walk and to trample.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 26a:14:1.hebrew: לאו משום דסבר כרבי יוסי הגלילי - דאמר בפירקין דלקמן (בבא קמא דף מב.), תם משלם חצי כופר ברה"ר:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 26a:14:1.english: [Is it] not because he holds like Rabbi Yosei HaGelili - Who says in our chapter below (Bava Kamma 42a) [that] an innocuous [ox] pays half [the] ransom in the public domain.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 26a:14:2.english: And he derives it - Rabbi Tarfon [derives it] for the domain of the injured party: full ransom.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 26a:14:3.hebrew: מק"ו מרגל - כי היכי דגמר לקרן תם לענין נזקין במתניתין. והכי גמר לה: מה שן ורגל, שפטורין ברשות הרבים לגמרי, ברשות הניזק — כופר שלם; קרן, שברה"ר חצי כופר כר' יוסי הגלילי, אינו דין שברשות הניזק — כופר שלם? מדגמר ר' טרפון הכי, אלמא איכא כופר ברגל, דאי לאו הכי, במאי מייתי לה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 26a:14:3.english: Via an a fortiori inference from Trampling - Just as he derived [the law of] the horn of an innocuous [ox] regarding damages in the Mishnah. And thus he derived it: If Tooth and Trampling, which are completely exempt in the public domain, [incur] full ransom on the property of the injured party; [then] Horn, which in the public domain [incurs] half ransom according to Rabbi Yosei HaGelili, is it not logical that on the property of the injured party [it incurs] full ransom? Since Rabbi Tarfon derived [it] thus, evidently there is ransom in [the case of] Trampling, for if not, from what would he derive it?

Rashi on Bava Kamma 26a:15:1.hebrew: מניזקין דרגל מייתי לה - ולעולם ליכא כופר ברגל, והכי גמר ר' טרפון: מה רגל שברשות הרבים פטור מנזקין, ברשות הניזק נזק שלם; קרן שברשות הרבים חצי כופר, כר' יוסי הגלילי, אינו דין שברשות הניזק כופר שלם:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 26a:15:1.english: He derives it from damages of Foot - And in truth, there is no ransom [payment] for Foot, and this is how Rabbi Tarfon derives [it]: Just as Foot, which in the public domain is exempt from damages, [pays] full damages in the domain of the injured party; [so too] Horn, which in the public domain [pays] half-ransom — in accordance with Rabbi Yosei HaGalili — is it not logical that in the domain of the injured party [it should pay] full ransom?

Rashi on Bava Kamma 26a:16:1.hebrew: שכן ישנו באש - תאמר בכופר שאינו באש, כדאמרינן בפ"ק (דף י.):
Rashi on Bava Kamma 26a:16:1.english: For it applies to Fire - Can you say [the same] regarding ransom, which does not apply to Fire, as we say in the first chapter (10a)?

Rashi on Bava Kamma 26a:16:2.hebrew: מטמון - שפטור באש וחייב ברגל, ומייתי לה הכי: מה רגל שברשות הרבים פטורה מכלום — חייבת ברשות הניזק אפילו על הטמון נזק שלם, קרן שברה"ר חצי כופר כו':
Rashi on Bava Kamma 26a:16:2.english: Concealed [articles] - which is exempt in [the case of] fire and liable in [the case of] trampling; and [the Gemara] derives it thus: just as trampling, which in the public domain is exempt from anything, is liable in the domain of the injured party even for concealed [articles] for full damages, [so too] horn, which in the public domain [is liable for] half-ransom, etc.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 26a:17:1.hebrew: שכן ישנו בבור - שאם היה גדי טמון בשק או במרצוף ונתגלגל ונפל לבור, חייב:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 26a:17:1.english: In that it applies to a pit - For if a kid was concealed in a sack or in a leather bag, and it rolled and fell into a pit, [the owner of the pit] is liable.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 26a:17:2.hebrew: מכלים - פטר בהו את הבור, ומכלים דרגל מייתי לה, וכדפרישית:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 26a:17:2.english: From vessels - [Scripture] exempted Pit regarding them, and [the Gemara] derives it from vessels [damaged by] Foot, and as I explained [above].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 26a:18:1.english: From concealed vessels - [That is, those] of Foot [Trampling], [from which one] derives it.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 26a:1:1.hebrew: חצי נזק קאמר - דתחייב כי קרן, דהא מקרן מייתי לה. וקרא דבשדה אחר לחיובי ביה ברשות הניזק נזק שלם אתא, דהכי משמע: בשדה אחר, נזק שלם:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 26a:1:1.english: He is saying half-damages - That [it] should be liable like Horn, for he derives it from Horn. And the verse of "in the field of another" comes to obligate it [for] full damages in the injured party's domain, for this is what it implies: "in the field of another" — full damages.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 26a:20:1.hebrew: א"ל רב אחא מדפתי כו' מה לניזקין דרגל שכן ישנו ברגל - תאמר בכופר, שאינו ברגל:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 26a:20:1.english: Rav Acha of Difti said to him, etc., "What [is unique] about damages of Trampling, in that it applies to Trampling?" - Will you say [the same] regarding ransom, which does not apply to Trampling?

Rashi on Bava Kamma 26a:22:1.hebrew: סימא את עין חבירו - אפי' בשוגג:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 26a:22:1.english: He blinded his fellow’s eye - Even unintentionally.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 26a:23:1.english: Just as [with] vessels, [the] four types of indemnity [do] not [apply] - For they do not apply to them.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 26a:23:2.english: So too, he blinded his fellow's eye - Unintentionally.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 26a:23:3.hebrew: נזק אין ארבעה דברים לא - דלא מחייבי ארבעה דברים אלא או מזיד או קרוב למזיד, דומיא דכי יריבון אנשים (שמות כ״א:י״ח), דהתם כתיב ריפוי ושבת:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 26a:23:3.english: [He pays for] damage, yes; [for] the four items, no - For one is not liable [for] the four items except [when acting] intentionally or close to intentionally, similar to "When men quarrel" (Exodus 21:18), for there healing and loss of livelihood are written.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 26a:2:1.english: The money of this [one] - [This refers to] Keren [goring].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 26a:4:1.hebrew: ישלם - מיטב שדהו ומיטב כרמו ישלם, לגמרי משמע:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 26a:4:1.english: He shall pay - “The best of his field and the best of his vineyard he shall pay” — [this] implies [paying] completely.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 26a:6:1.hebrew: אמר קרא יחצון - דקרא יתירא הוא, דנכתוב "וחצו את כספו וגם את המת", אלא לדרשא אתא, דאף ברשות הרבים נמי חייב:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 26a:6:1.english: The verse states: "They shall divide" - For it is a superfluous [word in the] verse, since [Scripture] could have written, "and they shall divide its money and also the dead [ox]"; rather, it comes for an exposition, that even in the public domain he is also liable.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 26a:7:1.hebrew: ויהא אדם חייב בכופר - כגון במזיד ולא אתרו ביה, דליתיה בר קטלא ולא בר גלות:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 26a:7:1.english: And let a person be liable [to pay] ransom - For example, where [he killed] intentionally and they did not warn him, so that he is neither subject to execution nor subject to exile.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 26a:7:2.english: And if an ox, which is not liable - for injury.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 26a:7:3.hebrew: ארבעה דברים - צער, ריפוי, שבת ובושת, אלא נזק לחודיה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 26a:7:3.english: Four things - Pain, medical costs, loss of livelihood, and humiliation; rather, [an ox is liable for] damage alone.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 26a:7:4.english: Liable [to pay] ransom - Where he killed him.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 26a:7:5.english: A person who is liable - etc.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 26a:8:1.hebrew: עליו ולא על האדם - על נזקי שור משלמין כופר, אבל על נזקי אדם אין משלמין כופר, אלא או מיתה או גלות:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 26a:8:1.english: Upon him, and not upon a person - For damages [caused by] an ox, one pays ransom [kofer], whereas for damages [caused by] a person, one does not pay ransom, but rather [is subject to] either death or exile.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 26a:11:1.hebrew: רגל שדרסה כו' - הוא הדין בשן דחיה דאורחה, הוה מצי למבעי, אבל בור ואש ממעטה מעליו, כמו אדם:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 26a:11:1.english: Trampling that trampled, etc. - The same applies to Tooth [damage] of a wild beast, which is its normal manner — [the Gemara] could have asked [about that as well], but Pit and Fire are excluded [from paying ransom] by [the word] "upon him," just like a person.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 26a:12:1.hebrew: או דלמא קרן כוונתו להזיק - תימה: מאי מספקא ליה? פשיטא דקרן חמירא מהאי טעמא, דליכא למימר דמקרן בק"ו יליף שאין מועד מתחילתו — דהשתא לא שייך למפרך [כדפרישית] במתניתין דאדם יוכיח שמועד מתחילתו ופטור מכופר. ועוד: היכי בעי למילף מקרן שכן חייבת ברשות הרבים:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 26a:12:1.english: Or perhaps, [with] Horn, its intent is to damage - This is astonishing: what is [the Gemara] uncertain about? It is obvious that Horn is more stringent for this [very] reason, for one cannot say that [Foot] is derived from Horn via a kal vachomer [on the grounds] that [Horn] is not forewarned from the outset — since now it is not applicable to refute [this, as I explained] in the Mishnah, that a human being proves [otherwise], as [a human] is forewarned from the outset yet is exempt from ransom. And furthermore, how could [the Gemara] seek to derive [Foot] from Horn, since [Horn] is liable in the public domain?

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 26a:14:1.hebrew: לאו משום דסבר לה כרבי יוסי הגלילי - וא"ת: אפי' בלא רבי יוסי הגלילי מק"ו גמר — ומה שן ורגל דפטורין ברה"ר חייבין בחצר הניזק כופר שלם, קרן לא כ"ש? וי"ל: דאם היה כופר חלוק מדין נזק, מדפטר ברה"ר לא הוה שייך למידן ק"ו:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 26a:14:1.english: Is it not because he holds in accordance with Rabbi Yosei HaGelili - And if you will say: Even without Rabbi Yosei HaGelili, he derives [it] via an a fortiori inference — just as Tooth and Foot, which are exempt in the public domain, are liable for full ransom in the yard of the injured party, is it not all the more so [for] Horn? And one can say: If ransom were distinct from the law of damages, [as seen] from the fact that [an innocuous ox] is exempt [from ransom] in the public domain, it would not be relevant to make [that] a fortiori inference.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 26a:14:2.hebrew: אלמא איכא כופר ברגל - והא דפליגי אביי ורבא בפרק שור שנגח ארבעה וחמשה (לקמן בבא קמא דף מא. ושם) ברגל שדרסה על גבי תינוק בחצר הניזק, דלרבא לא משלם כופר — אליבא דההוא תנא איירי, ולא משום דסבר רבא הכי:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 26a:14:2.english: Evidently, there is a ransom [payment] in [the case of] Trampling - And [as for] that which Abaye and Rava disagree in the chapter [entitled] Shor SheNagach Arba'ah VaChamishah (below, Bava Kamma 41a, and there) regarding a foot that trampled upon a child in the injured party's courtyard, where according to Rava [the owner] does not pay ransom — [Rava] is speaking according to that Tanna, and not because Rava himself holds thus.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 26a:1:1.hebrew: מידי כוליה ניזקא קאמרינן - וא"ת: "וביער" ע"כ לגמרי אתא לפטור, דנזק שלם מהי תיתי? לאו פירכא היא, דאי לאו "בשדה אחר", ממילא חייבת נזק שלם ברשות הרבים בלא קל וחומר:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 26a:1:1.english: Are we saying [that he pays] the full damage? - And if you ask: "[The verse] 'and it grazed' perforce comes to exempt [him] completely, for from where would [liability for] full damage come?" [The answer is that this] is not a refutation, for if not for "in the field of another," you would automatically obligate full damage in the public domain without an a fortiori inference:

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 26a:3:1.hebrew: ולא תהא שן ורגל כו' - וא"ת: הא אמר "כספו" — של זה ולא כספו של אחר? וי"ל, דאין למעט מ"כספו" אלא חצי נזק שמשתלם מגופו, ד"כספו" של זה — חצי נזק מגופו, ולא של אחר; וכאן, אם היה בחצר הניזק חצי נזק, הוה משתלם מן העלייה, אבל לעיל, אי הוי מחייב שן ורגל ברה"ר, הוה משתלם מגופו כמו קרן. וא"ת: היכי גמר הכא מקרן? מה לקרן — דין הוא שאפילו בחצר הניזק לא משלם אלא חצי נזק, שכן אין משתלם מן העלייה! ויש לומר: צרורות יוכיחו, שמשתלם מן העלייה לרב פפא (לעיל בבא קמא ג:), ואין משלם אלא חצי נזק. וא"ת: אי שן ורגל בחצר הניזק חצי נזק, אמאי איצטריך "כספו" — של זה ולא כספו של אחר? דהשתא ק"ו דלעיל ליכא! וי"ל, דאי לאו "כספו", הוה שבקינן ק"ו דהכא דמיקל בתשלומין, והוה עבדינן קל וחומר דלעיל דמחמיר בתשלומין:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 26a:3:1.english: And let Eating and Trampling [not be liable] etc. - And if you ask: Behold, [the Gemara] said "his money" — of this one, and not the money of another? And one can answer: [The Gemara] only excludes from "his money" half-damages that are paid from [the animal's] body, for "his money" of this one [means] half-damages from its body, and not of another; and here, if [Eating and Trampling] in the injured party's courtyard were [to pay] half-damages, it would be paid from the best [of the damager's property], whereas earlier, if Eating and Trampling had been held liable in the public domain, it would have been paid from its body like Goring. And if you ask: How can [the Gemara] derive [this] here from Goring? What [is special] about Goring — it is logical that even in the injured party's courtyard it pays only half-damages, since it is not paid from the best [property]! And one can say: Pebbles prove [otherwise], for according to Rav Pappa (above, Bava Kamma 3b), [pebbles] are paid from the best [property], and yet [one] pays only half-damages. And if you ask: If Eating and Trampling in the injured party's courtyard [were] half-damages, why would "his money" — of this one, and not the money of another — be needed? For now, the a fortiori inference from earlier does not exist! And one can answer: If not for "his money," we would have abandoned the a fortiori inference here, which is lenient with respect to payment, and we would have made the a fortiori inference from earlier, which is stringent with respect to payment.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 26a:7:1.hebrew: ויהא אדם חייב בכופר - מ"לא תקחו כופר לנפש רוצח" לא נפקא, דההיא (אמר) דאיצטריך דלא תשקול מיניה ממונא למפטריה, כדאמרינן בפרק אלו נערות (כתובות דף לז:), והכא איירי שיהרג וישלם כופר כמו השור. ומדתנא דבי חזקיה (שם דף לה.) לא נפקא אלא לפטור בשוגג בלא מתכוין כמו במזיד במתכוין, שזה כזה; אבל כופר באדם, כל זמן דלא אשכחן דפטור בשום מקום, לא מצינן למילף מיניה כלל:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 26a:7:1.english: And let a person be liable to pay ransom - [His exemption] is not derived from [the verse], "You shall not take ransom for the life of a murderer," for that [verse] is needed [to teach] that you may not take money from him to exempt him [from execution], as we say in the chapter Elu Na'arot (Ketubot 37b), whereas here [the Gemara] is speaking of [a case] where he is executed and pays ransom, just like the ox [which is stoned while its owner pays ransom]. And from [the teaching] of the school of Chizkiyah (ibid. 35a), it is only derived to exempt [him from monetary liability] in an inadvertent [act] without intent just as in an intentional [act] with intent, as this is like that; however, [with respect to] ransom for a person, as long as we have not found that he is exempt in any place, we cannot derive [his exemption] from it at all.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 26a:7:2.hebrew: אינו דין שחייב בד' דברים - וא"ת: מה לאדם שכן מועד מתחילתו? וי"ל דנזקי אדם מנזקי אדם יליף:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 26a:7:2.english: Is it not right that he is liable for the four [types of indemnity] - And if you ask: What [is the comparison] to a person, since [a person] is forewarned (mu'ad) from the outset? One can answer that it derives damages of a person from damages of a person.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 26a:8:1.hebrew: עליו ולא על האדם - בפרק החובל (לקמן בבא קמא דף פג:) דריש: "לנפש רוצח אי אתה לוקח כופר, אבל אתה לוקח כופר לראשי אברים", ופריך: והאי מבעי ליה דאמר רחמנא לא תעביד ביה תרתי, דלא תשקול מיניה ממונא ונקטליה? לאו בכופר דהכא איירי, דא"כ הוה ליה לשנויי: ההוא מ"עליו ולא על האדם" נפקא! אלא איירי בממון אחר בהדי מיתה, וטעי גמרא כדטעי באלו נערות (כתובות דף לז:), דקבעי גבי דרשה ד"לא יהיה אסון": "לא תקחו כופר לנפש רוצח" למה לי? כלומר, דמ"לא יהיה אסון" נפקא; אלמא ס"ד דמיירי בממון אחר בהדי מיתה:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 26a:8:1.english: “Upon him,” and not upon a person - In the chapter [entitled] HaChovel (later, Bava Kamma 83b), [the Gemara] expounds: “For the life of a murderer” — you may not take ransom [kofer], but you may take ransom for [the loss of] major limbs; and [the Gemara] asks: But is this [verse] not needed for what the Merciful One said: Do not do two things to him, [meaning] that you shall not take money from him and execute him? [That question] is not speaking of kofer as here, for if so, [the Gemara] should have answered: That is derived from “upon him, and not upon a person”! Rather, it is speaking of other monetary payment alongside execution, and the Gemara erred [in its initial assumption], just as it erred in [the chapter entitled] Eilu Na’arot (Ketubot 37b), where it asks regarding the exposition of “there is no fatality”: Why do I need “You shall not take ransom for the life of a murderer”? That is to say, [it assumed] that it is derived from “there is no fatality”; thus we see that it initially thought that [the verse] refers to other monetary payment alongside execution.
